title: Windowed reservoir prefill and decoder handoff: decouple reservation from decode scheduling
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed tail-latency spikes in mixed prefill/decode workloads when the prefill stage tried to reserve large contiguous token budgets for long-running decodes. The prior approach tightly coupled prefill reservation with immediate decode scheduling, which allowed single requests with deep generation to stall many concurrent short requests due to oversized reservations and KV cache pressure. This PR introduces a windowed reservoir abstraction that separates 'reservation' (how many tokens we will allow a request to claim in the near horizon) from 'decode scheduling' (when kernels are actually dispatched).

Design summary: introduce a reservoir manager that allocates token windows in small, time-bounded chunks (windows). Prefill now pre-allocates only the next N-window tokens (configurable, default 8 tokens/window) instead of attempting to reserve full generation length. A decoder handoff queue absorbs prefill completions and drives decode dispatch based on live scheduler signals (latency headroom, per-GPU token budget, KV memory pressure). Key components: reservoir.Manager, window_allocator, handoff_queue, decode_backpressure_probe. The reservoir supports opportunistic top-up and soft-eviction hints for KV cache to keep warm prefixes without monopolizing KV capacity.

Behavioral changes: - Prefill is now chunked by windows rather than by full-request length. - Decode dispatch can preempt queued decode work to honor short requests when latency SLOs are at risk. - KV cache retention uses reservation age + access frequency to decide soft-evict candidates.

Checklist: [x] Design doc updated with sequence diagrams (linked in PR) [x] Unit tests for reservoir allocation and handoff queue [x] Integration tests covering mixed short/long synthetic workloads [x] Benchmarks for 1/10/100 concurrent request mixes [x] Feature-flag guarded, default on in main on 2026-02-25

Benchmarks: On an internal T4-like staging cluster with mixed traffic (50% short 8-token, 50% long 1024-token), median P95 latency improved by 18% for short requests and overall GPU token throughput increased by ~9% compared to master. Tail P99 for short requests reduced from 320ms to 180ms. KV cache hit-rate for short prefixes increased by ~6 percentage points. Full benchmark outputs are attached to the issue/Linear ticket.

Operational notes and rollout: Enabled behind runtime flag runtime.windowed_reservoir.enabled. Gradual rollout plan: 10%->50%->100% over 72 hours with automated rollback if short-request P99 increases by >10% or if GPU memory usage increases >12%. Added a console dashboard tile to show reservoir occupancy, per-GPU window backlog and soft-evict events.

How to test locally: 1) Run unit tests: pytest tests/runtime/test_reservoir.py 2) Start runtime with feature flag on: RUNTIME_FLAGS=runtime.windowed_reservoir.enabled=true ./bin/runtime --config staging.yaml 3) Run mixed load harness: tools/loadgen/mixed_prefill_decode.py --short=8 --long=1024 --qps=200 4) Observe metrics: prefilling.window_fill_rate, handoff.queue_depth, decode.preemptions.

Compatibility: Backwards compatible with existing model kernels; changes are at scheduler layer and add a small per-request metadata field (reserved_windows) that is ignored by older control-plane components. No API changes to client surface.

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: mis-tuned window size could increase overall latency for very-long generative workloads. Mitigation: auto-tune probe that samples long requests and temporarily grows window size for hot streams. - Risk: soft-evict thrashing could cause cache churn. Mitigation: we use exponential decay on soft-evict score and retain a minimum warm quota per model instance.

Related work: builds on prior speculative prefill and chunked prefill experiments but explicitly decouples reservation and dispatch. See ENG-1147 design notes and earlier PRs for kernel coalescing and prefetch hints.

release_notes: Introduce windowed reservoir-based prefill to reduce tail-latency for short requests and improve overall token throughput. Feature-flagged and rolled out behind runtime.windowed_reservoir.enabled. See ops guide for rollout steps.
testing_notes: Unit and integration test coverage added. Repro harness available at tools/loadgen/mixed_prefill_decode.py. Watch metrics prefilling.window_fill_rate and handoff.queue_depth during canary. CI matrix includes linux-x86 integration and a sim-gpu job.
notes_for_ops: Rollback: set RUNTIME_FLAGS=runtime.windowed_reservoir.enabled=false and drain handoff queues by sending /admin/drain-handoff for nodes in the canary cohort. Monitor handoff.queue_depth and decode.preemptions during rollback.
